why: asset-lane4's audit (_workspace/current/engineering/asset-lane4-presentation-art-report.md §2.1) found zero dead image references but one real presentation gap: all nine StageCatalog entries collapsed onto three literal sprite names in GameDirector, so the loading screen never said which door was opening. GameDirector.StageCutsceneSprite now prefers 'scene-stage-entry-<stageId>' and falls back to the generic frame, which makes each file below a drop-in opt-in.
providerNote: The default private-codex backend returned HTTP 429 for every request on this machine (same failure already recorded in docs/provenance/scene-ember-rest.json). scene-stage-entry-cinder-span.png was generated by asset-lane5 through private-codex before the throttle closed; the remaining nine came through --provider codex-cli.
sizeHandling: codex-cli rejects --size, so the prompt asks for a wide landscape banner and each output is centre-cropped to 3:2 and resampled (PIL LANCZOS) to 1536x1024 — the resolution the shipped scene-*.png frames already use. Script: scratchpad gen2.sh (normalise()).
promptBase: WIDE LANDSCAPE horizontal banner composition, much wider than tall. Dark fantasy game loading-screen key art, painterly concept illustration, no text, no characters, no logos. Charcoal near-black stone architecture, volumetric fog, cinematic depth, dramatic rim light. The lower third stays visually calm and uncluttered because narration text is overlaid there.
promptBaseNote: The calm-lower-third clause exists because CutsceneView overlays kicker/title/narration there; the no-text clause because all copy is UI, not art.
accentSource: Per-stage accent colours are the ones already driving StageMood/floor tint, tabulated in _workspace/current/engineering/vfx-lane-w9-v2-v3-report.md §3.5.1.
